claim: BK channels are regulated by cytosolic Ca2+ and depolarizing voltages.
source: Since the BK channels are regulated by cytosolic Ca2+ and depolarizing voltages (Marty, 1981; Pallotta et al., 1981; Latorre et al., 1982), they are integrators of physiological stimuli involving intracellular Ca2+ elevation and membrane excitability.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to three published studies (Marty, 1981; Pallotta et al., 1981; Latorre et al., 1982).

claim: BK channels are integrators of physiological stimuli involving intracellular Ca2+ elevation and membrane excitability.
source: Since the BK channels are regulated by cytosolic Ca2+ and depolarizing voltages (Marty, 1981; Pallotta et al., 1981; Latorre et al., 1982), they are integrators of physiological stimuli involving intracellular Ca2+ elevation and membrane excitability.
evidence: This is inferred from the dual regulation by Ca2+ and voltage, which are key physiological signals.

claim: Different modules in BK channels harbor voltage and Ca2+ sensors that communicate allosterically with the channel gate.
source: Thus, different modules harbor voltage and Ca2+ sensors that communicate allosterically with the channel gate (Cox et al., 1997; Horrigan and Aldrich, 1999; Horrigan and Aldrich, 2002; Horrigan et al., 1999; Rothberg and Magleby, 1999; Rothberg and Magleby, 2000; Cui and Aldrich, 2000).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to published studies.

claim: Functional BK channels are formed by homotetramers of α-subunits.
source: Functional BK channels are formed by homotetramers of α-subunits (Shen et al., 1994), each comprising a transmembrane voltage-sensing domain (VSD) and an intracellular Ca2+-sensing C-terminal domain (CTD) that can independently modulate the ion conduction gate in the pore domain (PD) (Latorre et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published studies (Shen et al., 1994; Latorre et al., 2017).

claim: Each BK α-subunit comprises a transmembrane voltage-sensing domain (VSD) and an intracellular Ca2+-sensing C-terminal domain (CTD) that can independently modulate the ion conduction gate in the pore domain (PD).
source: Functional BK channels are formed by homotetramers of α-subunits (Shen et al., 1994), each comprising a transmembrane voltage-sensing domain (VSD) and an intracellular Ca2+-sensing C-terminal domain (CTD) that can independently modulate the ion conduction gate in the pore domain (PD) (Latorre et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Latorre et al., 2017.

claim: The CTDs consist of two non-identical regulators of the conductance of K+ domains (RCK1 and RCK2) arranged in a ring-like tetrameric structure dubbed the gating ring.
source: The CTDs consist of two non-identical regulators of the conductance of K+ domains (RCK1 and RCK2) arranged in a ring-like tetrameric structure dubbed the gating ring (Wu et al., 2010; Yuan et al., 2010; Yuan et al., 2012; Hite et al., 2017; Tao et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to published studies.

claim: Each RCK domain contains distinct ligand-binding sites capable of detecting Ca2+ in the micromolar range.
source: Each RCK domain contains distinct ligand-binding sites capable of detecting Ca2+ in the micromolar range (Schreiber and Salkoff, 1997; Bao et al., 2002; Xia et al., 2002).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published studies.

claim: In the absence of Ca2+, the activation of the VSD decreases the free energy necessary to fully open the BK channels in an allosteric fashion.
source: In the absence of Ca2+, the activation of the VSD decreases the free energy necessary to fully open the BK channels in an allosteric fashion (Horrigan and Aldrich, 1999; Horrigan et al., 1999).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published studies.

claim: With 0 Ca2+, very positive membrane potentials are required to drive all voltage sensors to their active conformations.
source: With 0 Ca2+, very positive membrane potentials are required to drive all voltage sensors to their active conformations (Cui et al., 1997; Stefani et al., 1997; Horrigan et al., 1999; Contreras et al., 2012), ultimately leading to near-maximal BK activation.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published studies.

claim: An appreciable open probability of BK channels at physiologically relevant voltages necessarily requires the activation of the Ca2+ sensors on the gating ring.
source: Thus, in cells such as neurons, an appreciable open probability of BK channels at physiologically relevant voltages necessarily requires the activation of the Ca2+ sensors on the gating ring.
evidence: This is inferred from the requirement of very positive potentials in the absence of Ca2+ and the physiological context.

claim: The voltage dependence of Ca2+-dependent gating ring rearrangements supports the idea that the energetic interaction between both specialized sensors may be crucial for BK channel activation.
source: The voltage dependence of Ca2+-dependent gating ring rearrangements (Miranda et al., 2013; Miranda et al., 2018) and RCK1 site occupancy (Sweet and Cox, 2008; Savalli et al., 2012; Miranda et al., 2018) as well as the perturbation of VSD movements by Ca2+ binding (Savalli et al., 2012) support the idea that the energetic interaction between both specialized sensors may be crucial for BK channel activation.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to multiple published studies.

claim: The physical CTD-VSD interface has been suggested to provide the structure capable of mediating the crosstalk between these sensory modules and their synergy in activating the pore domain.
source: The physical CTD-VSD interface has been suggested to provide the structure capable of mediating the crosstalk between these sensory modules and their synergy in activating the pore domain (Yang et al., 2007; Sun et al., 2013; Tao et al., 2017; Zhang et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published studies.

claim: The strength of the interaction between voltage and Ca2+ sensors and their relevance to BK channel activation is still debated.
source: However, the strength of the interaction between voltage and Ca2+ sensors and their relevance to BK channel activation is still debated (cf. Horrigan and Aldrich, 2002; Carrasquel-Ursulaez et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to conflicting studies.

claim: The RCK1 and RCK2 Ca2+-binding sites have distinct functional properties conferred by their different molecular structures and relative positions within the gating ring.
source: The RCK1 and RCK2 Ca2+-binding sites have distinct functional properties conferred by their different molecular structures and relative positions within the gating ring (Wu et al., 2010; Yuan et al., 2010; Yuan et al., 2012; Hite et al., 2017; Tao et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published studies.

claim: The RCK sites differ in their Ca2+ binding affinities.
source: Thus, the RCK sites differ in their Ca2+ binding affinities (Bao et al., 2002; Xia et al., 2002; Sweet and Cox, 2008), divalent cations selectivity (Oberhauser et al., 1988; Schreiber and Salkoff, 1997; Zeng et al., 2005; Zhou et al., 2012), voltage dependence (Sweet and Cox, 2008; Savalli et al., 2012; Miranda et al., 2018) and in their contribution to allosteric gating mechanisms (Yang et al., 2010; Yang et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published studies.

claim: Only the RCK1 site appears to be involved in communicating the Ca2+-dependent conformational changes towards the membrane-spanning VSD.
source: In particular, only the RCK1 site appears to be involved in communicating the Ca2+-dependent conformational changes towards the membrane-spanning VSD (Savalli et al., 2012; Miranda et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published studies.

claim: The Aplysia BK structure has revealed that the N-lobe of the RCK1 domain is in a non-covalent contact with the VSD and the S4-S5 linker that connects the voltage sensor to the pore domain.
source: Recently, the Aplysia BK structure has revealed that the N-lobe of the RCK1 domain is in a non-covalent contact with the VSD and the S4-S5 linker that connects the voltage sensor to the pore domain.
evidence: The claim is based on structural information from the Aplysia BK channel.

claim: The RCK1-VSD interaction surface is rearranged when comparing the liganded and Ca2+-free structures.
source: This RCK1-VSD interaction surface is rearranged when comparing the liganded and Ca2+-free structures (Hite et al., 2017; Tao et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to structural studies.

claim: It has been hypothesized that any Ca2+-induced rearrangements of the gating ring should ultimately be transmitted to the pore domain via the VSD.
source: In fact, it has been hypothesized that any Ca2+-induced rearrangements of the gating ring should ultimately be transmitted to the pore domain via the VSD (Hite et al., 2017; Zhou et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published studies.

claim: Ca2+ sensor occupancy has a strong impact on VSD activation through a coordinated interaction mechanism in which Ca2+ binding to a single α-subunit affects all VSDs equally.
source: Our results indicate that Ca2+ sensor occupancy has a strong impact on VSD activation through a coordinated interaction mechanism in which Ca2+ binding to a single α-subunit affects all VSDs equally.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on experimental data and modeling.

claim: The two distinct high-affinity Ca2+-binding sites contained in the C-terminus domains, RCK1 and RCK2, contribute equally to decrease the free energy necessary to activate the VSD.
source: Moreover, the two distinct high-affinity Ca2+-binding sites contained in the C-terminus domains, RCK1 and RCK2, contribute equally to decrease the free energy necessary to activate the VSD.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on experimental data from mutants.

claim: Voltage-dependent gating and pore opening in BK channels is modulated to a great extent by the interaction between Ca2+ sensors and VSDs.
source: We conclude that voltage-dependent gating and pore opening in BK channels is modulated to a great extent by the interaction between Ca2+ sensors and VSDs.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study based on the experimental findings.

claim: The IG-ON relaxation exhibits an almost complete decay before the IK achieves an exponential time course in 0 Ca2+ conditions.
source: The IG-ON relaxation exhibits an almost complete decay before the IK achieves an exponential time course in 0 Ca2+ conditions (Figure 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: The time constant of the IK activation is ~3.4 ms at 160 mV in 0 Ca2+ conditions.
source: Thus, the time constant of the IK activation (~3.4 ms at 160 mV) following a delay of ~160 µs is consistent with the movement of the voltage sensors preceding channel opening.
evidence: The claim is based on experimental measurements.

claim: The fast IG-ON relaxation reflects the movement of the gating charge in the channel's closed conformation, regardless of internal Ca2+ concentration.
source: Thus, the fast IG-ON relaxation reflects the movement of the gating charge in the channel's closed conformation, regardless of internal Ca2+ concentration.
evidence: This is inferred from the kinetic analysis of gating and ionic currents.

claim: The OFF-gating current was dramatically modified becoming smaller in amplitude and with slower kinetics as the internal Ca2+ concentration was increased.
source: Figure 2A shows that the OFF-gating current was dramatically modified becoming smaller in amplitude and with slower kinetics as the internal Ca2+ concentration was increased (see also Figure 2—figure supplement 1A and Figure 2—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2A and supplementary figures.

claim: At least two components (fast and slow components) could be resolved in the OFF gating current decay in 'zero' and 10 µM internal Ca2+ conditions.
source: At least two components (fast and slow components) could be resolved in the OFF gating current decay in 'zero' and 10 µM internal Ca2+ conditions (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B-C).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B-C.

claim: The time constants of the fast relaxation of the IG-OFF evoked at -90 mV are in reasonable agreement with the time constants values extrapolated to the same voltage from the two-state model of the IG-ON kinetic.
source: Figure 2—figure supplement 1D shows that the time constants of the fast relaxation of the IG-OFF evoked at -90 mV (open and closed orange circles) are in reasonable agreement with the time constants values extrapolated to the same voltage from the two-state model of the IG-ON kinetic.
evidence: The claim is supported by data and modeling shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1D.

claim: The relative contribution of the slower component increasing as internal Ca2+ is increased, reflecting an increase in the open probability of the channel.
source: On the other hand, the relative contribution of the slower component increasing as internal Ca2+ is increased, reflecting an increase in the open probability of the channel (Figure 2—figure supplement 1E-F).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1E-F.

claim: At applied voltages of -150 mV and -200 mV, the charge displaced in the ON is recovered in the OFF.
source: At these applied voltages, the charge displaced in the ON is recovered in the OFF (Figure 2—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2B.

claim: The standard HA model makes two simplifying assumptions: the model considers that there is a single Ca2+-binding site per α-subunit, and the model assumes the Scheme I as the Ca2+ binding-VSD interaction scheme.
source: It should be noted that the standard HA model makes two simplifying assumptions. First, the model considers that there is a single Ca2+-binding site per α-subunit. Second, the model assumes the Scheme I as the Ca2+ binding-VSD interaction scheme underlying the general gating mechanism of BK channel (Horrigan and Aldrich, 2002).
evidence: The claim describes the assumptions of the Horrigan-Aldrich model based on the cited reference.

claim: At extreme conditions of low (0.03 to 0.1 µM) and high (≥100 µM) internal Ca2+, VSD activation behaves in a mechanism-independent manner since all voltage sensors are in the same functional state (unliganded or saturated).
source: At extreme conditions of low (0.03 to 0.1 µM) and high (≥100 µM) internal Ca2+, VSD activation behaves in a mechanism-independent manner since all voltage sensors are in the same functional state (unliganded or saturated).
evidence: This is inferred from the modeling and experimental conditions.

claim: The Ca2+-binding effect on the VSD activation according to Scheme II is characterized by a five-component Boltzmann function.
source: By contrast, the Ca2+-binding effect on the VSD activation according to Scheme II is characterized by a five-component Boltzmann function (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C and Equation 6 in Appendix).
evidence: The claim is based on modeling shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Ca2+-binding is slow enough to safely ignore calcium re-equilibration during the 100 μs it takes to measure the gating charges.
source: Therefore, we can conclude that Ca2+-binding is slow enough to safely ignore calcium re-equilibration during the 100 μs it takes to measure the gating charges.
evidence: This is inferred from the simulations and kinetic analysis.

claim: The mutant M513I has been shown to eliminate the Ca2+ sensitivity mediated by the RCK1 site.
source: We also examined the effect of the mutant M513I (Bao et al., 2002) which has been shown to eliminate the Ca2+ sensitivity mediated by the RCK1 site (Bao et al., 2002; Bao et al., 2004; Zhang et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published studies.

claim: Both D362A/D367A and M513I mutations affect the Ca2+-induced enhancement of the activation of the voltage sensor very similarly through the RCK1 site.
source: Therefore, both mutations affect the Ca2+-induced enhancement of the activation of the voltage sensor very similarly through the RCK1 site (Figure 6C), although their mechanisms of action could be quite different.
evidence: The claim is based on comparison of experimental data from both mutants shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Both high-affinity Ca2+-binding sites contribute approximately equally to the decrease in free energy that is necessary to activate the VSD.
source: Therefore, both high-affinity Ca2+-binding sites contribute approximately equally to the decrease in free energy that is necessary to activate the VSD.
evidence: This is inferred from the similar effects of RCK1 and RCK2 site mutations on VSD activation.

claim: These findings reveal an additive effect of Ca2+-binding to the RCK1 and Ca2+ bowl sites on the VSD activation, which suggest independent allosteric pathways through which they exert their modulation on the VSD.
source: Remarkably, these findings reveal an additive effect of Ca2+-binding to the RCK1 and Ca2+ bowl sites on the VSD activation, which suggest independent allosteric pathways through which they exert their modulation on the VSD.
evidence: This is inferred from the equal and additive contributions of RCK1 and RCK2 sites.

claim: These results suggest that functional activation of the gating ring is propagated to the VSD, leading to structural perturbations of voltages sensors, thereby favoring its active conformation.
source: These results suggest that functional activation of the gating ring is propagated to the VSD, leading to structural perturbations of voltages sensors, thereby favoring its active conformation (Savalli et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is based on interpretation of fluorescence studies cited.

claim: The structural rearrangement of the gating ring in response to Ca2+ has a voltage dependence attributable to the operation of the voltage sensor.
source: Second, the structural rearrangement of the gating ring in response to Ca2+ has a voltage dependence (Miranda et al., 2013; Miranda et al., 2018) attributable to the operation of the voltage sensor.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published studies.

claim: Perturbations of pore opening equilibrium (e.g. through the F315A mutation or the assembly of BKα channel with γ1-subunit) does not modify the voltage-dependent reorganization of the gating ring.
source: In contrast, perturbations of pore opening equilibrium (e.g. through the F315A mutation or the assembly of BKα channel with γ1-subunit) does not modify the voltage-dependent reorganization of the gating ring (Miranda et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is based on experimental findings cited from Miranda et al., 2018.

claim: Proposing that the VSD and Ca2+ sites interact in the manner described by Scheme II reproduces reasonably well the behavior of the Ca2+-dependent gating charge movement observed in our experiments.
source: Proposing that the VSD and Ca2+ sites interact in the manner described by Scheme II reproduces reasonably well the behavior of the Ca2+-dependent gating charge movement observed in our experiments (Figure 4B–D).
evidence: The claim is based on comparison of model predictions with experimental data shown in Figure 4B–D.

claim: This concerted CTD-VSD communication may underlie a mechanism analogous to the mechanical strategy of interaction between the homooctameric ring of RCK domains and the pore module described for bacterial K+ channels.
source: This concerted CTD-VSD communication may underlie a mechanism analogous to the mechanical strategy of interaction between the homooctameric ring of RCK domains and the pore module described for bacterial K+ channels (Jiang et al., 2002; Ye et al., 2006; Lingle, 2007; Pau et al., 2011; Smith et al., 2012; Smith et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is speculative, drawing an analogy to bacterial K+ channels based on citations.

claim: In both MthK and BK channels the Ca2+-site occupancy triggers a conformational change corresponding to a symmetric overall rearrangement of the cytosolic tetrameric structure that is ultimately propagated to the transmembrane regions (TMD) via C-linker and in the BK channel, also via the protein-protein interfaces between the gating ring and the TMD.
source: In both MthK and BK channels the Ca2+-site occupancy triggers a conformational change corresponding to a symmetric overall rearrangement of the cytosolic tetrameric structure that is ultimately propagated to the transmembrane regions (TMD) via C-linker and in the BK channel, also via the protein-protein interfaces between the gating ring and the TMD (Jiang et al., 2002; Jiang et al., 2003; Ye et al., 2006; Yuan et al., 2010; Yuan et al., 2012; Pau et al., 2011; Smith et al., 2012; Tao et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to structural and functional studies.

claim: We can speculate that each Ca2+-binding event produces a gradual conformational expansion of the gating ring affecting the four voltage sensors in each step through the progressive perturbations within the protein-protein interfaces.
source: Thus, we can speculate that each Ca2+-binding event produces a gradual conformational expansion of the gating ring affecting the four voltage sensors in each step through the progressive perturbations within the protein-protein interfaces.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as speculation.

claim: The communication pathway through which the Ca2+-driven conformational changes are propagated to the voltage sensors appears to reside on the CTD-VSD interface that involves non-covalent interactions between RCK1 N-lobe and S0-S4 transmembrane segments.
source: As mentioned above, the communication pathway through which the Ca2+-driven conformational changes are propagated to the voltage sensors appears to reside on the CTD-VSD interface that involves non-covalent interactions between RCK1 N-lobe and S0-S4 transmembrane segments (Yang et al., 2007; Yang et al., 2008; Yang et al., 2010; Sun et al., 2013; Hite et al., 2017; Tao et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published studies.

claim: Binding of Ca2+ makes the RCK1 N-lobe pull on the S6 helix from its subunit whereas the modification of the contact surface between the RCK1 N-lobe with the voltage sensor of an adjacent subunit induces an outward displacement of the voltage sensor.
source: Therefore, binding of Ca2+ makes the RCK1 N-lobe pull on the S6 helix from its subunit whereas the modification of the contact surface between the RCK1 N-lobe with the voltage sensor of an adjacent subunit induces an outward displacement of the voltage sensor (Hite et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is based on structural information cited from Hite et al., 2017.

claim: Scanning mutagenesis of RCK1-N terminal subdomain indicates that residues on the βA-αC region are involved in the allosteric connection of the Ca2+-dependent activation mediated by RCK1 site occupancy.
source: Scanning mutagenesis of RCK1-N terminal subdomain indicates that residues on the βA-αC region are involved in the allosteric connection of the Ca2+-dependent activation mediated by RCK1 site occupancy (Yang et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a mutagenesis study.

claim: The selective activation of the RCK1 domain was identified as being responsible for the Ca2+-induced VSD rearrangement and the voltage dependence of the Ca2+-driven motions of gating ring.
source: In line with this study, the selective activation of the RCK1 domain was identified as being responsible for the Ca2+-induced VSD rearrangement (Savalli et al., 2012) and the voltage dependence of the Ca2+-driven motions of gating ring (Miranda et al., 2016; Miranda et al., 2018), suggesting that CTD-VSD allosteric coupling is primarily determined by the RCK1 site (Sweet and Cox, 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published studies.

claim: The constructs D362A/D367A and 5D5A selectively impair the Ca2+-sensitivity of the RCK1- and RCK2-sensors, respectively, by neutralizing the residues that are involved in contributing to Ca2+-coordination.
source: The constructs D362A/D367A and 5D5A (D894A-D898A) selectively impair the Ca2+-sensitivity of the RCK1- and RCK2-sensors, respectively, by neutralizing the residues that are involved in contributing to Ca2+-coordination (Zhang et al., 2010; Tao et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published studies.

claim: Comparing the fast gating charge movement at 0 Ca2+ and saturating Ca2+ conditions reveals that the energetic effect of Ca2+-binding on voltage sensor equilibrium is practically identical (~ −4 kJ/mol) for both the D362A/D367A and the 5D5A mutations.
source: Comparing the fast gating charge movement at 0 Ca2+ and saturating Ca2+ conditions reveals that the energetic effect of Ca2+-binding on voltage sensor equilibrium is practically identical (~ −4 kJ/mol) for both the D362A/D367A and the 5D5A mutations (Figure 5).
evidence: The claim is based on experimental data from mutants shown in Figure 5.

claim: Our findings establish that the RCK2-driven contribution to CTD-VSD energetic coupling is quite similar to the RCK1-driven contribution.
source: Thus, our findings establish that the RCK2-driven contribution to CTD-VSD energetic coupling is quite similar to the RCK1-driven contribution.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on experimental data from mutants.

claim: The M513I mutation hinders the Ca2+-dependent activation associated with the RCK1-sensor, presumably by disrupting the structural integrity of the binding site and the transduction pathway through the βA-αC region.
source: This point mutation hinders the Ca2+-dependent activation associated with the RCK1-sensor, presumably by disrupting the structural integrity of the binding site and the transduction pathway through the βA-αC region (Zhang et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a published study.

claim: We found that the energetic contribution of each RCK site to the voltage sensor equilibrium is the same and its combination mimics the VSD Ca2+-sensitivity of the fully occupied sites.
source: We found that the energetic contribution of each RCK site to the voltage sensor equilibrium is the same and its combination mimics the VSD Ca2+-sensitivity of the fully occupied sites.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on experimental data from mutants.

claim: Our results suggest that the two RCK-sensors contribute independently to the modulation on the VSD, although we cannot eliminate the possibility of some cooperativity between them.
source: Thus, our results suggest that the two RCK-sensors contribute independently to the modulation on the VSD, although we cannot eliminate the possibility of some cooperativity between them.
evidence: This is inferred from the additive effects of the two sites.

claim: Various lines of evidence indicate that there is some, albeit modest, cooperativity between the two high-affinity Ca2+-binding sites although its nature is still unclear.
source: Indeed, various lines of evidence indicate that there is some, albeit modest, cooperativity between the two high-affinity Ca2+-binding sites although its nature is still unclear (Qian et al., 2006; Savalli et al., 2012; Sweet and Cox, 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published studies.

claim: Intra and intersubunit structural connectivity supports the putative cooperative interactions between the Ca2+ sensors at the gating ring.
source: Intra and intersubunit structural connectivity supports the putative cooperative interactions between the Ca2+ sensors at the gating ring (Hite et al., 2017; Yuan et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to structural studies.

claim: A recent functional study of the intrasubunit connections between the RCK1 site and Ca2+ bowl (R514-Y904/E902 interactions) has shown that such connections are potential candidates for the structural determinants underlying a cooperative mechanism between the RCK1- and RCK2-sensor.
source: In fact, a recent functional study of the intrasubunit connections between the RCK1 site and Ca2+ bowl (R514-Y904/E902 interactions) has shown that such connections are potential candidates for the structural determinants underlying a cooperative mechanism between the RCK1- and RCK2-sensor.
evidence: The claim is based on a recent functional study.

claim: These interactions are involved in either the preservation of the integrity of RCK1 Ca2+-binding site or define the allosteric propagation pathway of the chemical energy induced by Ca2+ binding towards transmembrane domains.
source: These interactions are involved in either the preservation of the integrity of RCK1 Ca2+-binding site or define the allosteric propagation pathway of the chemical energy induced by Ca2+ binding towards transmembrane domains (Kshatri et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a published study.

claim: Based on the cryo-EM structure of Aplysia californica BK channel, it has been proposed that there should be a positive cooperativity between the Ca2+-binding at RCK1 site and the Ca2+ bowl since the Ca2+-induced conformational change of the RCK1-N lobes from closed to open configuration depends on the functional state (unliganded and liganded) of both RCK sites.
source: On the basis of the cryo-EM structure of Aplysia californica BK channel, (Hite et al., 2017) proposed that there should be a positive cooperativity between the Ca2+-binding at RCK1 site and the Ca2+ bowl since the Ca2+-induced conformational change of the RCK1-N lobes from closed to open configuration depends on the functional state (unliganded and liganded) of both RCK sites.
evidence: The claim is based on structural information and proposal from Hite et al., 2017.

claim: The analysis of our gating current data when using cooperativity between the two high-affinity sites produced a result at odds with previous reports.
source: In fact, the analysis of our gating current data when using cooperativity between the two high-affinity sites (Table 1) produced a result at odds with previous reports.
evidence: The claim is based on model fitting results shown in Table 1.

claim: Functional studies point out a more relevant role of the intrasubunit cooperativity (albeit modest) than the intersubunit cooperativity between the RCK Ca2+ sites.
source: However, functional studies point out a more relevant role of the intrasubunit cooperativity (albeit modest) than the intersubunit cooperativity between the RCK Ca2+ sites (Niu and Magleby, 2002; Qian et al., 2006).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to functional studies.

claim: Although a concerted CTD-VSD model (Scheme II) gives better explanation than an independent CTD-VSD model (Scheme I) to the allosteric communication of the calcium and voltage sensors, more work is required to explore improved models able to reproduce more accurately the properties of the interaction CTD-VSD mechanism in BK channel.
source: Thus, although a concerted CTD-VSD model (Scheme II) gives better explanation than an independent CTD-VSD model (Scheme I) to the allosteric communication of the calcium and voltage sensors, more work is required to explore improved models able to reproduce more accurately the properties of the interaction CTD-VSD mechanism in BK channel.
evidence: This is a concluding statement acknowledging limitations and future directions.

source: The cDNA coding for the human BK α-subunit (U11058) was provided by L. Toro (University of California, Los Angeles, CA).
evidence: This is a methodological detail about the source of materials.

claim: The cDNA coding for independent mutants of each two high-affinity Ca2+ site from BK channel were kindly provided by M. Holmgren (National Institutes of Health, Bethesda, MD).
source: The cDNA coding for independent mutants of each two high-affinity Ca2+ site from BK channel, the double mutant D362A/D367A (Xia et al., 2002), the mutant M513I (Bao et al., 2002) in the RCK1 Ca2+-binding site, and the mutant 5D5A (Schreiber and Salkoff, 1997) (D894A/D895A/D896A/D897A/D898A) in the RCK2 Ca2+-binding site or calcium bowl, were kindly provided by M. Holmgren (National Institutes of Health, Bethesda, MD).
evidence: This is a methodological detail about the source of materials.

claim: Xenopus laevis oocytes were used as a heterologous system to express BK channels.
source: Xenopus laevis oocytes were used as a heterologous system to express BK channels.
evidence: This is a methodological detail about the expression system.

claim: All recordings were made by using the patch-clamp technique in the inside-out configuration.
source: All recordings were made by using the patch-clamp technique in the inside-out configuration.
evidence: This is a methodological detail about the recording technique.

claim: Gating current (IG) records were elicited by 1 ms voltage steps from −90 to 350 mV in increments of 10 mV.
source: Gating current (IG) records were elicited by 1 ms voltage steps from −90 to 350 mV in increments of 10 mV.
evidence: This is a methodological detail about the experimental protocol.
